public_sources.title: Wang et al., SCARCE: Scalable Cascade Analysis for Rare-event Characterisation via Embeddings
observed_results: SCARCE replaces a handcrafted subset-simulation performance function with learned embeddings plus geometric rulers and adaptive quantile thresholds. For a target probability around 1e-5, the paper contrasts roughly 1e7 simple-Monte-Carlo forward passes for 10% relative error with roughly 1e5 total samples for a typical rho=0.1 subset-simulation configuration N=20000.
On MNIST misclassification, SCARCE reports roughly 400-500x lower mean absolute error than grid-searched traditional subset simulation and removes systematic over-counting in that benchmark.

For Llama-Guard-3-8B PAIR-style fleet jailbreak estimation, a PCA ruler reports 2.6% mean relative error for adversarial fraction eta>=1e-3 versus finite-sample references whose average bootstrap relative half-width is 27.9%; after recalibration it reports 2.93% relative error on a GCG-style corpus.

The anytime-valid upper envelope is conditional on a conservative level-estimator assumption E[p_hat_l|past]<=p_l. Exact stationarity of the within-level MCMC gives equality; the authors state the weaker condition accommodates O(1/N) adaptive-subset bias and is empirically satisfied in their experiments.

In LLM use the ruler-defined surrogate event is not treated as the target label. The cascade estimates P(A_tau), and labelled calibration estimates precision/recall so P(T)=P(A_tau)*precision/recall. The paper explicitly notes geometric separability is observed empirically, not imposed as a guaranteed property.

Directional KL between good and bad ruler-score distributions has Spearman rho=0.83 with estimation error over only six ruler families; the paper marks this as preliminary and notes the small family grid.

public_sources.title: Lin et al., Toward a Principled Framework for Agent Safety Measurement
observed_results: BOA searches both within an LLM turn and across a multi-turn agent-environment interaction tree, pruning trajectories below a user-chosen length-relative likelihood budget and returning a likelihood-weighted safety score over the in-budget trajectory set.

It uses chunk expansion, breadth-first block-tree traversal, batching, prefix-cache reuse and chunked judging to make multi-turn search tractable. On 72 Agent-SafetyBench prompts and four models, it surfaces concrete unsafe trajectories that greedy decoding labels safe and gives graded scores where greedy produces one bit.

Per-prompt experiments use a 600-second budget. Reported average costs are 92.9K/6.7K/12.8K/1.1K generation tokens and 358/122/139/190 seconds for Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-32B and Llama-3.1-70B respectively; the paper describes most token budgets as roughly equivalent to 10-20 ordinary samples.

BOA's target is explicitly likelihood-budgeted trajectory-space safety, not the unrestricted deployment distribution. Environment responses are treated as deterministic conditional on tool calls in the formalization. Budget-exhausted leaves are completed with rollout averages, so finite-budget output should not be conflated with an unbiased rare-event estimator over all trajectories.

derived_results.claim: SCARCE supplies a concrete answer to the r106 score-design frontier: use learned representations to construct a progress ruler when no scalar failure coordinate exists, but keep representation/ruler, cascade sampler and target-event calibration as separate components. The calibration step is essential; a geometrically convenient surrogate event is not automatically the semantic failure event.

A learned/adaptive subset cascade can have an anytime-valid one-sided envelope, but the guarantee is not free: it requires conservative conditional level estimates (stationarity gives exact unbiasedness). A local adaptation should therefore expose MCMC mixing/level bias as a first-class certificate rather than invoking 'anytime-valid' solely because thresholds are adaptive.

BOA and importance/splitting estimators solve different endpoints. BOA is strong for systematic discovery/ranking inside a likelihood-budgeted multi-turn trajectory tree; AVF, twisted SMC and subset simulation are stronger templates when the output must be a calibrated probability under a specified base distribution. A useful evaluation stack should not report search coverage or explored-trajectory safe fraction as if it were an unbiased deployment risk estimate.

For replayable agent evaluation, branch at semantic environment transitions and cache shared prefixes so rare-trajectory search reuses deterministic/common history rather than paying full rollout cost after every perturbation. BOA provides direct multi-turn systems evidence for batching, prefix reuse and chunked expansion; probability-valid sampling methods can potentially use the same execution substrate while retaining their own weights/estimators.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Both SCARCE and BOA are 2026 arXiv preprints. Their reported performance and formal scopes should not be treated as established peer-reviewed consensus.
SCARCE's supermartingale envelope assumes conservative conditional level estimates; arbitrary adaptive MCMC or poor mixing can violate that condition.

SCARCE's LLM probability relies on a calibrated surrogate event. Precision/recall calibration can drift under a new target distribution and must be re-estimated; the paper itself recalibrates on GCG-style transfer.
The directional-KL ruler selection result has n=6 ruler families and is preliminary.

BOA searches an epsilon likelihood-budgeted trajectory set and uses a finite compute budget. Its experimental safety score should not be exported as an unbiased estimate of total deployment failure probability.
BOA formalizes environment responses as deterministic given tool calls; stochastic or partially observed environments require a modified probability model.
No AGI capability conclusion follows. These are evaluation/search mechanisms.

candidate_update.rare_event_score: strengthened with representation-aware ruler construction plus explicit semantic calibration and mixing/bias condition
candidate_update.multi_turn_agent_evaluation: new route: systematic likelihood-budget trajectory search with prefix caching/chunked expansion, explicitly separated from probability-valid risk estimation

frontier: Search for a method that combines multi-turn trajectory-tree search/replay with an importance-weighted or splitting estimator of the unrestricted base-distribution failure probability; BOA alone is search-budgeted and AVF/SCARCE are not full tool-agent tree methods.
Find empirical tests of SCARCE or related learned-reaction-coordinate subset simulation under poor MCMC mixing / representation shift, and quantify when the conservative-level condition fails.
Find a learned-evaluator multifidelity/control-variate study where score calibration and high-fidelity correction are both explicit, with cost-normalized variance reduction on an ML-system task.
Design a local evaluation interface with four separately logged objects: semantic target label, progress/ruler score, sampling/search proposal, and final calibrated probability estimator.
exact_next_action: Prioritize a bridge between BOA-style multi-turn branch search and probability-valid rare-event estimation: look for trajectory-space importance sampling, sequential Monte Carlo or splitting that supports stochastic/replayable agent-environment states and explicit likelihood weights. If absent, derive a minimal composition where BOA-like prefix caching is only an execution optimization underneath AVF/SMC weights, leaving the estimator unchanged. In parallel examine SCARCE's mixing/bias condition and representation-transfer failure modes rather than adding another ruler family.
